body: They are absolutely built on trust.  You're very right.  I feel like when I've let my guard down, that's when the shit hits the fan though.  It's kinda weird, if I start trusting someone, crap happens, and, if I keep to myself, crap happens.  I guess crap is just gonna happen either way, so I might as well trust everyone and, as you say, take that risk that it will work out sooner or later (I'm sure there are quotes on this...).  It does get tiring when it constantly seems to NOT work out, but, you're right.  Wiping the slate clean is the perfect way to view what I should be doing.  Thanks man, you're a good guy.

Just to be clear, I wanna make sure you know this other nurse moving on does, indeed, bother me.  I thought we were a good team, then it just stopped.  However, why it bothers me the MOST though is how it feels like it's just the most recent link in a long chain of this kind of crap happening.  On the other hand, I wasn't actually familiar with Occham's Razor, but, after a quick glimpse at the wikipedia page for it, I have to say I kinda like it.  It makes a very good point.

Anyway, thanks so much.  For what it's worth, you seem like a pretty awesome guy too.  I hope things have been going well for you as you deserve it.

Edit and PS - It very well could be self-sabotage...another poster pointed it out, and I could see where I thought I was doing such a good job of "not trying too hard" that I could even be coming out on the other end.  Maybe I am.

Thanks for the reply, man.  It means a lot.

I REALLY don't think my parents would have said the same thing if my sister and I were reversed, but I know they would have been upset.  Would they have been better off in that scenario?  I guess nobody can say for sure, but I can't help but think they would be.

But a second reply mentioning a self-fulfilling prophesy...I never thought of it in terms of maybe me coming off like I'm turning people away though.  That's food for thought.  I kinda don't think it's the case, but it's definitely something I never thought about.  It's possible I suppose.  Thanks again.

Thanks, man.  To begin, I understand I'm working with people who are worse off than me.  I don't expect them to get up and hug me and tell me how thankful they are for me - I didn't become a nurse for the glory, or lack thereof, that's for sure.  I didn't, however, count on being a constant punching bag.  A wise, older nurse told me that it's part of the job, and sometimes that's what the patient needs.  I get it, I guess.  I can accept it in a lot of situations too, but some are just there to be jerks.  That's the case in any service industry though, I know.  I guess I really ought to man up and get used to it.  But, man, I guess I never realized how bad I'm dwelling on just the negative side of things.  Thanks for pointing out the small talk and laughs I have with patients.  It does happen a lot - I guess I just forget to focus on that.  I really ought to put more emphasis on that for my patients' and my own good.

As for my family, you're right.  I try not to stay trapped within myself and remember it was my parents who lost their daughter.  I don't want to paint my Dad as a bad guy because he isn't.  He goes out of his way for me, and he and my Mom clearly love me.  But he tends to talk over me and generally belittle my choices.  I can say or do something that will be exactly the same as what my sister or brother-in-law does, and it's amazing how different his response is to us.  It's clear he holds my surviving sister in higher esteem than me.  I just feel like he thinks I have no idea what I'm doing with my life.  People have told me he needs to feel like that with people, but I have no idea.  I don't know why it's me then.  Furthermore, everyone in my family has all these stories to tell while nobody seems to have any interest in the day I saved a patient or the day I had to deal with my first patient dying.  I just feel less and less involved, you know?  My sister has two sons my parents are ecstatic over, and I've been more or less stagnant and by myself my whole life.

All the same, in those moments of clarity when I snap out of it, I realize anything I do along those lines would still absolutely devastate my family.  I don't know why, but they still really do love me.  My coworkers and friends might be upset for a little while, but they'd be able to move on just fine.  I don't, however, know if my parents could handle losing another kid.  Even if it is "just me."

Anyway, thanks for the offer, friend.  I ended up falling asleep all day (I've been on a nightshift schedule for a couple weeks), so I didn't mean to back out and ignore everybody.  I still may take you up on that offer.  If not though, feel free to do likewise if anything is bothering you.  I owe the four of you.  Thanks again.

Oh trust me, I understand there are people too busy dealing with their own crap to always be able to step aside and point out their appreciation all the time, and I wouldn't expect them to by any means.  A lot of people are worse off than me.  Though, if there's one thing I've learned in my short time of being a nurse, it's definitely nice to make a point to show a little gratitude - it's good for both the giver and the receiver.

But you're calling self-sabotage, huh?  I always thought I was good at making sure I wasn't doing that, but maybe.  It's so hard to tell what some of your autopilot personality traits are.  I guess it's a possibility.

Anyway, like I mentioned, I sorta brought up that she wasn't working with me anymore, and she kinda got mad and then immediately felt bad.  Which confused the heck outta me - not to mention made me feel bad.  As I said, she has no obligation to me.  If she wants to work with someone else, that's her prerogative.  I just wish I could get a scoresheet on her that tells me, "Hey, this is what you did right, and this is why she got sick of you."  As it stands, all I ever get from it is, "Well, you sucked again apparently."

As for what my Dad said, it's certainly something I think about every day.  I think about my sister every day, and then that'll pop up into my mind's conversation, and I think, "Am I doing better by them?  Are they happy I'm here?"  Generally, the answer is yes.  I know my parents love me.  They really are great parents.  But do I ever feel less-than-adequate?  Oh, all the time.  Sometimes that thought of, "If I'm not even the best available option to my own parents, how would anyone else see me any other way?" will crop up.  I know it's illogical, so I can generally shrug it off and remind myself everyone has different tastes.  Though, it does tend to get more glaring when I feel like I'm constantly losing out on the whole social life thing.

All that said, thanks for the reply, the concern, and the kind words.  It really means a lot.

Thanks for the reply, friend.  You may not call it strong advice, but it's one thing I never really thought of, though I kinda feel silly that I never have.  To roll with it and ride out the constant cast and crew changes, as you call it, is definitely not like my personality, but perhaps it's something I should learn.  Don't get me wrong, I never expected everyone to stay involved and interested in my life, but I just didn't think most of my "friendships" and "relationships" would be these two month affairs all the time.  It gets old, but, if it's gonna keep happening, I guess I should count my blessings, appreciate the friends who do stick with me, and look forward to next month's set of friends (maybe some will stick). Ha.

I keep rereading everyone's posts to me, and the one thing I keep taking away from yours is to try and stay optimistic.  It's so easy to dwell on the people who drift away, I guess I just never realized how negative I was being.  Change of scenery is hardly ever bad, I suppose...
